eniac.name: ENIAC and punch cards
eniac.description: Computing without a screen: 18,000 tubes, lamps as the only output, and programs punched into cardboard.

visual.body: Programming meant physically rewiring the machine. No screen, no keyboard, no operating system — a room-sized calculator rebuilt by hand for every new problem.

batch.name: Mainframes and batch processing
batch.description: The first operating system appears, because humans are far too slow to hand out machine time by hand.

unix.name: UNIX
unix.description: Green phosphor, a blinking cursor — and for the first time a person can talk to the machine directly.

lines: for the first time an operating system
Small programs that each do one thing,
Every command typed in a terminal

dos.name: IBM PC and MS-DOS
dos.description: The computer moves into the office, and everything has to fit into 640 kilobytes of memory.

visual.dirVolume: Volume in drive C is AHMADOS
visual.body: Computers arrive on desks. One program at a time, one screen, everything typed. 640 kilobytes of memory — which, contrary to the famous quote nobody can actually source, everyone knew would not be enough for long.

macintosh.name: Macintosh
macintosh.description: An arrow on the screen changes everything: windows, icons, menus, and a mouse in your hand.

win95.name: Windows 95 and dial-up
win95.description: Start menu, taskbar, and a modem screeching its way onto the internet.

cloud.name: Cloud, containers and AI
cloud.description: The machine is everywhere and nowhere: dashboards, containers, and rules that decide where packets may go.
